evidence: Ov. Met. 14.532: alimentaque cētera flammae (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 14.5: alimentīs ignium (Lewis & Short, s.v. molestus)
terms.comment: Its first sense is food, nourishment; for fuel it takes a genitive, ignis or flammae, and in the poets is always plural (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens (s.v. fuel) has the plural for the fuel of machines too (Egger).

evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.17.26: suggerunt affatim ligna proximae silvae
terms.comment: The household fuel: ligna are logs for the fire, as against māteria, timber for building (Lewis & Short, s.v. māteria). See wood.
Traupman’s phrase; Egger has liquor prōpulsōrius (M-O s.v. fuel). For a car, petrol is benzīnum (see petrol).
Dry stuff to catch a spark; in Christian Latin, figuratively, the tinder of sin.

phrases.latin: picem et cērās, alimentaque cētera flammae
phrases.english: pitch and wax and everything else that feeds a flame
the nearby woods supply plenty of firewood

sources: Lewis & Short: alimentum · Lewis & Short: lignum · Lewis & Short: materia · Lewis & Short: fomes
